title: Java4Shell Vulnerability Puts Many Enterprise Applications at Risk of Takeover
content_md: Oracle and the OpenJDK project have patched Java4Shell, a critical Java runtime vulnerability that researchers say can be exploited to hijack popular enterprise applications without authentication. The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-114938, is a memory safety flaw in the way OpenJDK processes Base64-encoded data. Calif, whose researcher Quang Luong discovered the bug, made its findings public on November 17, after news of the flaw surfaced ahead of the coordinated disclosure. Specifically, the bug was found in a routine that OpenJDK relies on to decode Base64 on x86-64 CPUs supporting AVX-512 VBMI. Calif’s analysis shows that invalid Base64 strings can cause the routine to write past the end of its output buffer, potentially corrupting nearby heap data before Java flags the input as invalid. “With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution,” Calif explained . The researchers call the memory leak capability JavaBleed. They warn that heap data exposed this way could contain PII, secret keys and tokens. Default configurations exposed to Java4Shell attacks In its initial tests, Calif achieved pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) on Keycloak, Atlassian Jira and Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, all running with default settings. Authenticated attackers could also execute code on Apache Kafka Broker, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker, and the researchers say neither list
